title: Keep the nightly usage export running for every tenant

blocks.text: Every night `UsageExport` writes one line per tenant for the billing system, such as `initech;quota=2500;jobs=1234`. Two tickets are open against it. Last night the job stopped halfway with an exception, at the first contract tenant whose contract has no quota. And billing rejects lines where a count of jobs has a decimal point in it.
`line(...)` already builds the line. Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/UsageExport.java`:

items: `quota(tenant)`: `100` for a tenant on the free plan, otherwise the quota in its contract, or `null` when the contract sets none;
`value(metric)`: an `Integer` for a count, a `Double` for a ratio.

blocks.text: Both are small choices between two values. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a free tenant gets 100 and a contract tenant gets the quota its contract sets
a ratio is exported as a Double
a contract tenant with no quota gets null and an 'unlimited' line, without an exception
a count is exported as an Integer, written without a decimal point

origin.section: A Conditional Expression Takes Its Type From Both Branches, So a Primitive on One Side Unboxes the Other

concepts: A conditional expression with an int and a double operand has type double, so an int result comes out as a Double.
A conditional expression with an int on one side and an Integer on the other has type int, so a null Integer throws NullPointerException where if/else would return null.
